DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilq.qov.ph DILG OPINION NO. 122 s. 2021 OCT 28 2021 ATTY. JAN ELSON G. ORQUILLAS City Legal Officer Office of the City Legal Office El Salvador City, Misamis Oriental Dear Atty. Orquilas: This has reference to your letter dated 20 August 2021 requesting for the Department's legal opinion concerning the filling up the permanent vacancy in the Sangguinang Barangay. Based on the letter, the attendant circumstances are as follows: A Sangguniang Barangay Member of Barangay Taytay, El Salvador City died. As such, the Sangguniang Barangay issued a resolution recommending a certain person to be appointed to the 7th position on the premise that the said person is qualified being a former candidate who lost in the previous barangay elections. When the local chief executive of the city was about to appoint the person recommended by the sanggunian, the child of the deceased sangguniang barangay member filed an administrative case before the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) of El Salvador City against the barangay officials, assailing the process of deliberation and recommendation. The complaint allegedly contended that the members of the sangguniang barangay who voted in favor of the recommended person received a certain amount of money from the latter. However, the SP of El Salvador City dismissed the administrative case for lack of probable cause. Again, as the local chief executive was about to proceed with the appointment of the person recommended after the dismissal of the administrative case, the legal counsel of the complainant sent a letter manifesting that they intend to refile the case against the barangay officials. Consequently, you raised the following issues: I. Whether or not the local chief executive can proceed with the appointment despite receipt of the letter with the intent to file a case disputing the recommendation process that transpired before the sangguniang barangay and despite being required to exercise due diligence in the performance of his duty. 2. Whether or not the "recommendation" requirement provided in Section 45(3) of R.A. 7160 presupposes that there should be no objection over the process. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

3. Can the local chief executive remand the matter to the Sangguniang Barangay to resolve the issue on recommendation and conduct a new deliberation involving interested parties? 4. What court, tribunal, or body has jurisdiction in the event the child of the deceased sangguniang barangay member will refile the administrative case in connection with the disputed recommendation. The first three questions will be discussed simultaneously since they are interrelated. The death of s Sangguniang Barangay Member created a permanent vacancy where automatic succession does not apply. The provisions under Section 45 of the Local Government Code of 1991 finds in application, viz: Section 45. Permanent Vacancies in the Sanggunian. - (a) Permanent vacancies in the sanggunian where automatic succession provided above do not apply shall be filled by appointment in the following manner: xxxx xxxx (3) The city or municipal mayor, in the case of sangguniang barangay, upon recommendation of the sanqquniang barangay concerned. (b) Except for the sangguniang barangay, only the nominee of the political party under which the sanggunian member concemed had been elected and whose elevation to the position next higher in rank created the last vacancy in the sanggunian shall be appointed in the manner hereinabove provided. xxxx Based on the foregoing, the city or municipal mayor is the appointing authority for vacant permanent positions in the sangguniang barangay, upon the recommendation of the sangguniang barangay. The recommendation by the sanggunian barangay takes the place of nomination by the political party since members of the sanggunian barangay are prohibited to have party affiliations, and is considered a condition sine qua non for the validity of the appointment. 1 Please take note that this Department has issued an opinion2 regarding the duty of the appointing authority on the filling up of permanent vacancies, to wit: "The first sentence of above-quoted Section 45 expressly provides the mandate to fill the permanent vacancies in the sanggunian where automatic succession does not apply. The word "shall" used in the said provision of the Local Government Code of 1991 is imperative, operating 1 Antonio Nachura, Outline Reviewer in Political Law, Quezon City, VJ Graphic Arts, Inc., page 754 DILG Legal opinion NO. 37 s.2015, September 22, 2015 2 of 4

to impose a duty which may be enforced. Hence. where a clear duty is imposed upon a public official. an unnecessary and unreasonable delay in the exercise of such duty or failure to comply such mandate shall be punishable under the law." (Emphasis ours) It is categorical in the aforementioned that the appointment by the city or municipal mayor is mandatory and recommendation of the concerned barangay is also mandatory being an element in the process of the appointment by the local chief executive. 3 When the Sanggunian of Barangay Taytay issued a resolution containing the name of the person recommended to fill in the permanent vacancy, the City Mayor of El Salvador City can proceed with the appointment. This is despite receipt of the letter with the intent to file a case disputing the recommendation process since it is the duty of the local chief executive to fill the permanent vacancy in the sanggunian barangay without unnecessary and unreasonable delay. The duty of the Mayor to appoint him/her is mandatory. Please be reminded that it was not the qualification of the recommended person to fill in the permanent vacancy in the Sangguniang Barangay that is being questioned, but the proceedings in which the Sangguniang Barangay concluded thereto. As to the fourth query, Section 67 of the Local Government Code of 1991 finds in application, to wit: Section 67. Administrative Appeals. - Decisions in administrative cases may, within thirty (30) days from receipt thereof, be appealed to the following: (a) The sangguniang panlalawigan, in the case of decisions of the sangguniang panlungsod of component cities and the sangguniang bayan; and xxxx xxxx xxxx Considering that the Sanggunian Panlungsod dismissed the case for lack of probable cause, the complainant may file an appeal to the Sangguniang Panlalawigan within thirty (30) days from the time he/she received the decision of the Sangguniang Panlungsod. The complainant may file the case with the Office of the Ombudsman who has concurrent jurisdiction with Sanggunian Panlungsod over administrative cases against elective barangay officials occupying positions below salary grade 27.4 The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. 3 DILG Opinion No. 24 s. 2019 dated June 10, 2021 Office of the Ombudsman vs. Rolson Rodriguez, G.R. No. 172700, July 23, 2010. 30f4

Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHOR F THE SECR MA . INO U e cretary for Barangay Affairs OUSBA/MBD/LLLS-LRALLDnasnvcwgms CC•. Dir. ARNEL M. AGABE. CESO Ill, Regional Director of DILG Region X 4 of 4
